Promotion
pro-mō'shun
n. (advancement in rank or honour; in Scripture always traced to God's hand rather than to man's striving)
Latin promovere, to move forward. The Hebrew in Psalm 75 is rum, to lift up or exalt; in Proverbs 3:35 the noun is used ironically of what fools actually receive.

Biblical Definition

“For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south” (Psalm 75:6). The sentence is famous for the direction it omits. Three points of the compass are ruled out and the fourth is not named, because the answer is not a direction at all but a Person, supplied in the next verse: “But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another” (Psalm 75:7). Advancement is judicial, an act of the Judge, and He both raises and lowers. Proverbs turns the word with heavy irony: “The wise shall inherit glory: but shame shall be the promotion of fools” (Proverbs 3:35). The fool is promoted — he rises, he becomes conspicuous — and what he is elevated into is shame. The proper way to seek advancement is given in the same book, and the agent is wisdom rather than the man: “Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her” (Proverbs 4:8). A man exalts wisdom and wisdom promotes him. The order is never reversed.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines promotion as advancement in station or honor, preferment, and exaltation in rank or dignity.

expand to see more

PROMOTION, n. The act of promoting; advancement; preferment in rank or honor.

2. Exaltation in honor or dignity, or in rank.

PROMOTE, v.t. To forward; to advance; to contribute to the growth, enlargement or excellence of any thing.

2. To exalt; to elevate; to raise; as, to promote an officer.

PREFERMENT, n. Advancement to a higher office or dignity.

Key Scripture

Psalm 75:6 — "For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south."

Psalm 75:7 — "But God is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another."

Proverbs 3:35 — "The wise shall inherit glory: but shame shall be the promotion of fools."

Proverbs 4:8 — "Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her."

Modern Corruption

Advancement is treated as a thing to be engineered, and Psalm 75 says the compass has no direction that supplies it.

expand to see more

The whole apparatus of self-advancement — the personal brand, the positioning, the network worked with an eye to what it can yield — assumes that promotion comes from somewhere on the map. Psalm 75:6 rules out three directions and leaves the fourth unspoken because the answer is above. This is not an argument for passivity; Scripture commends diligence and says that a man diligent in his business shall stand before kings. It is a denial that the outcome is in the striver's hands. Joseph in prison, David keeping sheep, and Daniel refusing the king's meat were all promoted, and not one of them arranged it.

Proverbs 3:35 supplies the sharpest warning, and it applies inside the church as much as outside. Shame shall be the promotion of fools — the fool is genuinely elevated, and elevation is precisely his punishment, because it puts his folly where everyone can see it. Ministries have watched this happen: a man is advanced beyond his character, and the promotion does not correct the deficiency but publishes it. That is one reason the New Testament requires an elder to be proved first, and forbids a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew rum, to be high, to exalt — Psalm 75:6-7; ruwm in the causative of God setting up and putting down; Proverbs 3:35 and 4:8 use the honour-vocabulary of the wisdom books.

expand to see more

Hebrew rum — to lift up, to exalt; Psalm 75:6-7, both of the promotion sought and the God who grants it.

Hebrew shaphel — to bring low; the counterpart in Psalm 75:7, he putteth down one and setteth up another.

Hebrew qalon — shame, dishonour; Proverbs 3:35, the promotion the fool actually receives.

Hebrew salal — to exalt, to lift up as a highway; Proverbs 4:8, exalt her and she shall promote thee.

1 Timothy 3:6 gives the New Testament caution: not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.

Usage

"“Promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south” — and the fourth direction is a Person."

"“Shame shall be the promotion of fools” — the elevation is itself the punishment."

"“Exalt her, and she shall promote thee” — the order is never reversed."
